components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: var(--font-condensed); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; font-size: 0.875rem; background: var(--color-terracotta); color: var(--color-cream); border: 1px solid var(--color-terracotta-dark); border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px 16px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), transform 180ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), box-shadow 180ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-terracotta-dark); transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 16px 28px -20px rgba(152,62,39,0.9); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: none; box-shadow: none; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-terracotta); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.css: .ds-field { display: grid; gap: 6px; width: 280px; } .ds-field-label { font-family: var(--font-condensed); font-size: 0.75rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.12em; color: var(--color-muted); } .ds-input { font-family: var(--font-body); font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--color-ink); background: rgba(255,248,233,0.92); border: 1px solid var(--color-line); border-radius: 4px; padding: 8px 12px; transition: border-color 160ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), box-shadow 160ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--color-faint); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--color-terracotta); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(188,78,49,0.18); }

components.css: .ds-nav { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 4px; border-radius: 6px; background: #101721; } .ds-nav-link, .ds-nav-soon { font-family: var(--font-condensed); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.08em; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 4px; color: #ead8bf; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-nav-link:hover { background: rgba(188,78,49,0.3); color: var(--color-cream); } .ds-nav-link.is-active { background: var(--color-terracotta); color: var(--color-cream); } .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-sand); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-nav-div { width: 1px; height: 16px; margin: 0 4px; background: rgba(234,216,191,0.2); } .ds-nav-soon { color: rgba(234,216,191,0.4); display: inline-flex; gap: 6px; align-items: center; } .ds-nav-soon em { font-style: normal; font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.1em; padding: 1px 6px; border-radius: 9999px; border: 1px solid rgba(234,216,191,0.2); color: rgba(234,216,191,0.6); }

narrative.overview:
Pentagramma looks like the printed programme handed out at a jazz concert: warm paper stock, a Bodoni masthead, condensed capitals for section labels, and one ink color doing all the shouting. Each screen is a page you read top to bottom, not a dashboard of floating widgets. The "jazz" lives in the contrast between the daytime paper where work is read (lists, forms, availability) and the night-club navy where things happen (header, the new-lesson panel, login).

Density is moderate. These are working screens used every day by office staff, teachers and families, on desktop and phone alike, so scanability comes before ornament. The brand shows in precise details: the type pairing, a single terracotta voice, hairline rules the color of aged paper, and long soft shadows that lift sheets off the desk.

The system rejects SaaS defaults: no pill buttons, no glassmorphism, no gradient text, no icon-plus-heading card grids, no kicker labels above headings.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground with a faint printed grain; navy reserved for chrome and action panels.
Terracotta is the only accent: primary actions, active navigation, page titles, "today".
Four-voice type: Bodoni display, Crimson headings, Nunito body, Oswald labels.
Nearly square corners (4px) and 1px paper-colored rules.
Times and dates set in tabular figures, like a printed schedule.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Terracotta is the only saturated hue on a paper screen. Ardesia and Salvia show up only as status tints, never as decoration.

rules.name: The Day/Night Rule
rules.body: Paper is for reading and reviewing. Blu Notte is for chrome and for the main creation action on a page. A screen never has more than one navy panel besides the header.

rules.name: The Small Capitals Rule
rules.body: Oswald is for labels and controls, never for running text or headings. Buttons are always uppercase Oswald, tracked 0.08em.

rules.name: The Printed Schedule Rule
rules.body: Every time, date range and count uses tabular figures (the `.tabular` utility).

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No eyebrow labels above headings. The heading carries its own weight; context goes in a line below it.

rules.name: The Sheet Rule
rules.body: Only top-level panels carry a shadow. Rows, chips and fields inside a panel are separated by rules and tone, never by shadows of their own.

dos: Do keep Terracotta to one primary action per panel plus the active or "today" markers (The One Voice Rule).
Do set every time, date range and count in tabular figures.
Do group schedule data by day under Crimson day headings, with hairline-divided rows.
Do use the `surface-paper` / `surface-dark` panels and the `btn-*` / `field-theme` classes rather than restyling controls ad hoc.
Do write all UI copy in Italian with correct accents (Lunedì, Disponibilità, già).
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Animations already collapse to 1ms globally.
donts: Don't add eyebrow or kicker labels above headings.
Don't nest bordered cards inside cards. Use rules and tone inside a panel.
Don't use pill-shaped buttons, glass or blur effects, gradient text, or a colored border-left above 1px.
Don't introduce a second saturated accent color.
Don't put Seppia or Filetto text on Blu Notte. Labels on navy use Sabbia.
Don't add unlayered global CSS resets (`* { margin: 0; padding: 0 }`). In Tailwind v4 they override every spacing utility.
